hints.title: Forward Sequence Coupling
hints.text: Choosing which balloon to burst first changes who its neighbors are for every later step, so the two sides stop being independent. What choice would keep the sides independent?

hints.title: Inverting Time to Last Burst
hints.text: Consider which balloon in a range is burst last; at that moment its neighbors are fixed, so the left and right parts become independent subproblems.

hints.title: Interval Recurrence Relation
hints.text: Pad the array with 1 at both boundaries and let dp[i][j] represent the maximum coins from bursting all balloons strictly between index i and j. For intervals of increasing length, compute dp[left][right] by testing each balloon k between left and right as the last burst, taking the maximum of dp[left][k] + dp[k][right] + nums[left] * nums[k] * nums[right].

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Interval DP iterating over all sub-ranges and last popped balloon k.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Choosing balloons in forward order means bursting balloon i couples its left and right neighbors across all future choices, destroying optimal substructure. A brute-force search over all N! permutations for N = 300 requires 300! ≈ 3 * 10^614 operations, which is completely intractable.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Allocating an O(N^2) dynamic programming table (dp[i][j] for all intervals (i, j)) enables solving the inverted problem (choosing the LAST balloon to burst) in O(N^3) operations by decoupling the subproblems.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Explaining clearly why forward DP fails (neighbor dependency) and why reverse DP works (last balloon burst maintains fixed boundary neighbors nums[left] and nums[right]); padding array with boundary 1s.

solutions.approach: Reverse Order Thinking (Choose LAST burst balloon in interval)
